textbookBox.concept: To add large numbers, keep the digits lined up: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: To add large numbers, keep the digits lined up: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands.
beats.speakEn: To add large numbers, keep the digits lined up: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands.

beats.en: A place on the corridor is 1,855 km from Srinagar and 1,862 km from Kanniyakumari. Add: 5 + 2 = 7 ones, 5 + 6 = 11 tens, so write 1 and regroup 1 hundred, and so on. The total is 3,717 km.
beats.speakEn: A place on the corridor is 1,855 km from Srinagar and 1,862 km from Kanniyakumari. Add: 5 + 2  equals  7 ones, 5 + 6  equals  11 tens, so write 1 and regroup 1 hundred, and so on. The total is 3,717 km.

type: Key Concept: To add large numbers, keep the digits lined up: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds

textbookBox.concept: When ten of one place is collected, we regroup it into one of the next place. Ten tens make one hundred.

beats.en: When ten of one place is collected, we regroup it into one of the next place. Ten tens make one hundred.
beats.speakEn: When ten of one place is collected, we regroup it into one of the next place. Ten tens make one hundred.

beats.en: The same method works for 5-digit numbers. Mahesh spent Rs 21,880 on fuel and toll and Rs 38,900 on other expenses: 21,880 + 38,900 = Rs 60,780.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 5 maths · We the Travellers (II) · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: To subtract, line up the digits and regroup when the top digit is smaller. A ship sails 2,700 km from Mumbai to Chennai by sea. After 1,083 km it reaches Cochin, so 2,700 - 1,083 = 1,617 km are left.

beats.en: Let us review the key takeaway from We the Travellers (II): To subtract, line up the digits and regroup when the top digit is smaller. A ship sails 2,700 km from Mumbai to Chennai by sea. After 1,083 km it reaches Cochin, so 2,700 - 1,083 = 1,617 km are left.
beats.speakEn: Let us review the key takeaway from We the Travellers (II): To subtract, line up the digits and regroup when the top digit is smaller. A ship sails 2,700 km from Mumbai to Chennai by sea. After 1,083 km it reaches Cochin, so 2,700 - 1,083  equals  1,617 km are left.

type: Summary: To subtract, line up the digits and regroup when the top digit is smaller.
